tasks.prompt: We are handing the colorama project over to a new team next month. Who actually wrote the Python code that is in the repository today, and how exposed are we if the two biggest contributors stop answering our questions?
tasks.ppInvokedPrompt: Use the /project-pilot:bus-factor command for this. We are handing the colorama project over to a new team next month. Who actually wrote the Python code that is in the repository today, and how exposed are we if the two biggest contributors stop answering our questions?
criteria: Top two owners. PASS: Jonathan Hartley is named top owner with 51-59% of surviving Python lines (truth 55.2%), and Arnon Yaari is named second as ONE person (his names/addresses merged, including wiggin15) with 9-15% (truth 12.0%). FAIL: Hartley outside 51-59%; Dana Kessler (or anyone other than Arnon Yaari) named second; Arnon's identities listed as separate people with none of them reaching 9%.

Formatter, vendored code, bots. PASS: the answer's own numbers give Dana Kessler (who ran the formatter and added the vendored module) at most 3% of the lines (truth 0.7%, 14 lines), and it states or clearly implies that the vendored colorama/_vendor lines (about 1,100) and the formatter/bot rewrites were not counted as authorship. FAIL: Dana Kessler at 10% or more, or presented as a major owner; any bot (pre-commit-ci, dependabot) credited with surviving lines; the vendored module counted as someone's code without a flag.

Revert/re-apply and applied patch. PASS: Priya Nair is credited with her cursor helpers and Windows Terminal helper (about 28 lines, 1.0-2.0%) although Jonathan Hartley committed the "Reapply" commit, and Tomas Ibarra is credited with the winterm clamp patch (about 15 lines) although Hartley committed it; if the answer lists contributors down to 1% it must include Priya. FAIL: Priya's lines credited to Hartley or reported as 0; Tomas Ibarra's patch credited to Hartley (committer); Priya missing from a list that goes below 1%.

Bus factor and exposure. PASS: the answer says that Hartley alone holds more than half of the surviving lines, so the bus factor is 1 (a statement that the smallest set reaching 50% has one person is enough), and that the top two together hold 63-71% (truth 67.2%). FAIL: bus factor stated as 3 or more; top-two share below 60% or above 74%; Hartley and Arnon not identified as the top two.

People who left. PASS: the answer names Nathaniel J. Smith (about 10%) and Delgan (about 5.5%) as no longer active (no commits for years), reports that the lines owned by people with no commit in the last 12 months are 25-35% of the code (truth 29.9%), and does not list Hartley, Arnon Yaari, Priya Nair, Tomas Ibarra or Dana Kessler as having left. FAIL: Smith or Delgan described as active; share of lines owned by departed people below 20% or above 40%; Hartley or Arnon described as having left.

criteria: time.go. PASS: Paul Borman (all his names/addresses merged: Paul Borman, pborman, <email redacted>, <email redacted>) is named main author of time.go with 65-80% of its lines (truth 73%) and described as no longer active (last commit 2023). FAIL: Sam Okafor (line-ending commit) credited with time.go; no single main author because Paul's identities are split; Paul Borman described as active.

version7.go and the committer/author split. PASS: MikeWang is named main author of version7.go with 72-90% (truth 81%), and Mei Chen is credited with the Time7 accessor, about 9% of the file (6-13%), although Ravi Menon committed it; Ravi Menon is not credited with Mei's lines. FAIL: Ravi Menon credited with the Time7 patch or with more than 5% of version7.go; Mei Chen missing while the answer discusses who wrote the file's recent additions.

SQL code across the rename. PASS: the answer follows the history of database_sql.go (formerly sql.go) and names Justin Overfelt as the largest author with 36-52% of the file (truth 44%), with Andrew Stone, David E. Wheeler and Daniel Souza as other original authors, all gone. FAIL: Ravi Menon (who did the rename) named as author or owner of the SQL code; the answer says the SQL code has no history or starts in 2025.

Who is still around. PASS: the answer says that almost all lines of the repository (93-98%, truth 95.9%) are owned by people with no commit in the last 12 months, that none of the three files has an active author with a meaningful share (time.go at most 8%, version7.go at most 3%, SQL code 0%), and that the only active people are Ravi Menon, Alex Rowe and Kofi Mensah, with Alex Rowe counted as ONE person (Alex Rowe, arowe and Alexander Rowe merged; about 92 lines, 3%). FAIL: Paul Borman, MikeWang or Justin Overfelt recommended as an available reviewer without saying they left; Alex Rowe listed as three people; a share of lines owned by departed people below 85%.

Noise that must not count. PASS: Noor Haddad (two commits, reverted ULID work) is credited with 0 surviving lines and not named an owner or expert; Sam Okafor owns no code (line-ending, generated and vendored changes); the bot commits are not treated as a person; Kofi Mensah is treated as active (his commit is dated Dec 2025 by the committer date, the 1970 author date is a clock error). FAIL: Noor Haddad or Sam Okafor named as owner/expert or given 1% or more; generated/vendored files counted as authorship; Kofi Mensah described as inactive since 1970.

criteria: Top owner. PASS: Felix Queissner / "xq" / MasterQ32 (all addresses and spellings merged) is named top owner with 43-52% of surviving lines (truth 47.2%) as one person. FAIL: the top owner shown below 40% because the spellings/addresses are listed separately; Tobias Ek or Wen Li named a top owner.

Mechanical changes do not create owners. PASS: Tobias Ek (split and move of files) is at most 2% (truth 0.3%) and Wen Li (rename/revert/re-apply of allocator to gpa, generated width table, width helper) is at most 2.5% (truth 1.5%, 24 lines); the answer says the help-printing code in help.zig remains attributed to its original authors (jnagpaul about 49% of it, Dhole about 23%). FAIL: Tobias Ek or Wen Li at 5% or more; help.zig credited to Tobias Ek; the generated width table counted as code anyone wrote.
